raw_response:
I farm 6 mu, so I do not play around too much. If I lose yield, that hurts more than spending a bit extra on fertilizer. I usually start from what I did last year and then look at water, fertilizer price, and what the men around me in the village are doing. Here in Quzhou County, with well water, wheat-maize is steady if I keep the timing tight and do not save too much on base fertilizer. I finished 30 years in the field, and with my primary schooling I do pay some attention to balance, not only urea. For wheat, I will keep improved seed, put enough base phosphorus, and split nitrogen so the crop stays strong through winter and greens up well in spring. With irrigation, I will water at sowing if the soil is dry, then around jointing, and again at filling if needed. For maize after wheat, I will use hybrid seed, because that is what gives yield here when water is available. I will not cut nitrogen too hard on maize, but I will still put some phosphorus and potassium so it does not grow all stalk and no grain. On 6 mu, family labor can manage it, so I will stay with rotary tillage after harvests because it is quick and cheaper than deep ploughing every season. I will spray wheat about 3 times in a normal year and maize 2 times, more only if worms or disease come badly.
